<reason>High-quality debate on both sides, but A (CON) built the more durable path to victory by arguing the motion as written. A's opening framed the burden cleanly: "only" makes all three conditions individually necessary, so CON needs just one to fail. A then defended that frame through every round: appeal was conceded as floor from the start (defusing B's capture), work was shown substitutable via reception support (A4.1's functional line — error-correction has no substitute, destitution does — directly answered B's best pressure question), and family unity was attacked as non-necessary for the median single-adult transfer, with B's "rules apply blindly" defense rebutted by A's point that ties surface at pre-transfer interviews — a point B never answered. B's capture strategy (your exception is an enforceable family right; your support guarantee is a smuggled right) was creative and forcefully pressed, but A's scalpel-vs-system distinction survives on the motion's text (destination countries must provide the rights), and A's closing flipped B's closing dilemma: either horn denies that the specific trio is necessary. B also claimed in Rebuttal 2 that A "never drew the line" on substitutes — premature, since A drew it explicitly in the very next turn, and B never engaged the drawn line afterward. Both sides were well-grounded (Rwanda, Hungary, Canada STCA, Dublin clauses) with no fake precision; both had one clipped turn, costing each a final punch but not the substance. B was rhetorically vivid and genuinely threatening, but A answered every material pressure point and closed the arithmetic: three necessary conditions promised, one defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's A4.1 functional-line answer to B's substitute challenge (appeal protects error-correction, which only review can secure; work protects against destitution, which reception support secures by other means) dissolved B's sharpest pressure question and anchored A's whole case; A's closing then flipped B's enforceable-or-discretionary dilemma so both horns "gore the same word" — only.</best_rebuttal>
